data.description: Found during the 72d9 CI-hang investigation (faulthandler-proven). Mechanism: _fetch_origin prefers a blobless partial fetch (--filter=blob:none, src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py fetch site). On a checkout that is itself shallow (CI: git init + fetch --depth=1), materialize_tickets/materialize can therefore resolve a ref whose blobs are absent, and _materialize_tree's git read-tree / git checkout-index --all (repo_snapshot.py:447-461) then triggers git's promisor lazy fetching — one HTTPS round trip per missing object batch — with no timeout anywhere (run_git's timeout parameter defaults to None and no caller passes one). Observed: a single checkout-index blocked >15 minutes per test and hours per CI lane. A production rebar MCP server running from a shallow or partial clone can hang the same way. Expected: local-looking materialization must fail fast (or fetch missing objects in ONE batched, bounded operation) instead of unbounded lazy fetching. Suggested directions: set GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 (git >= 2.43) in _materialize_tree's env so a missing object errors immediately with an actionable message; and/or pass explicit timeouts on network-capable run_git call sites; and/or detect a shallow/promisor repo in acquire() and surface a descriptive SnapshotError. Acceptance criteria: (1) materializing a tree whose blobs are absent from a partial clone fails within seconds with a descriptive error naming the remedy, pinned by a unit test using a --filter=blob:none clone fixture; (2) no run_git call on the materialize path can block indefinitely (timeout or GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH), asserted by test; (3) make lint, make typecheck, and the default suite exit zero.
data.title: materialize/_materialize_tree can lazy-fetch unboundedly on a partial clone (no run_git timeout): local-looking git ops hang for hours
